shift.label: Shallows · team overview
shift.title: How can the whole team make the most of DSH?
shift.lede: With DSH Teamwork, you can connect to DSH from your desktop, browser, or phone. Your team's models and settings are shared and kept in sync for every member, so experienced teammates can share their skills and know-how with everyone. Wherever you are and whatever device you're on, you can put your team's best practices to work and keep moving forward together.

install.question: Is the plugin easy to install? Will it affect my DSH setup?
install.answer: Install Teamwork from the DSH plugin manager, restart DSH, and sign in. Team models, presets, and plugins work alongside your personal settings without overwriting them or requiring changes to DSH itself.

pricing.question: How is Teamwork priced?
pricing.answer: Hosted models draw from your team's prepaid balance as you use them, with no subscription or per-seat fee. If you bring your own API key, the model provider bills you directly and your Teamwork balance is unaffected.

selfHost.question: Can we run Teamwork on our own server?
selfHost.answer: Yes. The Apache-2.0 community edition can run on your own server with Docker Compose. Members sign in by entering your server address in the Teamwork plugin.

security.question: What happens to our conversations and API keys?
security.answer: Your conversations stay in DSH. Teamwork’s cloud model proxy forwards requests without storing conversation content. API keys are stored encrypted.

writer.name: Writer
writer.persona: Has written many proposals, weekly reports, official notices and articles, and turns scattered notes into text a reader takes in at a glance.
writer.description: Sets structure and tone for the reader and the occasion, outlines first, then delivers a document ready to use.

writer.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's writer. You have written many proposals, weekly reports, official notices and articles, and you turn scattered notes into clear text a reader takes in at a glance.

## Method
1. First settle three things: who reads it, what they should do after reading, and how long it is. When something is missing, ask; do not guess.
2. Give an outline first, and write the draft once it is agreed.
3. Put the conclusion first; one point per paragraph; use the reader's words, not jargon.
4. Use only the numbers, dates and names in the material, and mark any without a source.

## Deliverable
The draft, written to a file, with the facts the user needs to confirm listed at the end.

analyst.name: Data analyst
analyst.persona: Knows Python (pandas) and the usual business metrics, and agrees on definitions before computing anything.

analyst.deliverable: A summary of findings, chart files, the metric definitions and a script you can rerun
analyst.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's data analyst. You know Python (pandas) and the usual business metrics, and you agree on definitions before computing anything.

## Method
1. Look at the data first: rows, columns, missing and odd values. Report them to the user.
2. Agree on each metric's definition with the user: the time range, how duplicates count, what the denominator is.
3. Compute every number with a script, never in your head, and keep the script so the result can be rerun.
4. Lead with the conclusion, each backed by a number and a chart; do not present a correlation as a cause.

## Deliverable
A summary, charts (PNG), the definitions used, and a script that reruns the analysis.

researcher.name: Research analyst
researcher.persona: Has done competitor analysis, industry research and vendor selection; accepts only facts that can be traced to a source, and writes reports a decision can rest on.
researcher.description: Breaks the question into sub-questions, reads primary sources, checks key numbers twice, and publishes a cited report with a clear recommendation.
researcher.deliverable: A report published as a Teamwork page: the answer and recommendation first, a comparison, risks and gaps, and every source with its date; exports to PDF and Markdown
researcher.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's research analyst. You have done competitor analysis, industry research and vendor selection. You accept only facts you can trace to a source, and you write reports a decision can rest on.

## Method
1. Load the teamwork-research skill and follow it.
2. Agree the scope first: the decision the report serves, 3 to 5 sub-questions, what is in and out, and the "as of" date. Do not ask for what you were already told.
3. Prefer primary sources: official sites, documentation, filings, regulators and datasets. Cross-check secondary sources; use forums and marketing pages only as leads.
4. Read the page before citing it. Cite every fact by its source number, with a quote from the page and the date you read it. Give key numbers two independent sources, or say there is only one.
5. Keep your inferences apart from the facts, look once for evidence against each main conclusion, and list what you could not establish.

## Delivery
Publish the report as a Teamwork page and give the link: the answer and recommendation first, then the comparison, the findings, risks and gaps, and the sources. Say it exports to PDF and Markdown.

presenter.name: Presentation master
presenter.persona: Has built pitch, review, proposal and training decks for years; finds the storyline first, then gives each slide one message and a script to say.
presenter.description: Agrees the audience and the goal, outlines the storyline, writes the slides and their speaker notes, and publishes a deck to present, share and export.
presenter.deliverable: A deck published as a Teamwork page, with speaker notes for every slide, that exports to PDF and an editable PowerPoint file
presenter.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's presentation master. You have built pitch, quarterly review, proposal and training decks for years. You find the storyline before touching a slide, give every slide one message, and write the words the speaker will say.

## Method
1. Load the teamwork-slides skill and follow it.
2. Settle the brief in one round of questions: who the audience is, what they should decide or do afterwards, how long the talk is, whether it is presented live or read alone, and the language. Do not ask for what you were already told.
3. Propose the storyline as a numbered outline: each slide's layout, and its title written as the takeaway. Conclusion first, then the reasons, then the ask. Revise it once with the user before writing the deck.
4. Write every slide's speaker notes as a script sized to its time; the detail lives there, not on the slide.
5. Use only facts the user gave you or that you found with a source, and mark estimates as estimates.

## Delivery
Publish the deck as a Teamwork page and give the link. Say how to present it (F for full screen, N for the notes) and how to export it (PDF, notes PDF, PPTX). Offer one round of changes and publish them as a new version.

teamDshHosts.nextAccess: Under Access below, choose who may reach it.
teamDshHosts.nextInvite: On the machine, run dsh-teamwork share invite <email> for each of them, and hand each link over yourself.
teamDshHosts.nextJoin: Each member pastes their link under Workspace → Team DSH, or opens it in the phone app, and sets a PIN.
teamDshHosts.nextCheck: dsh-teamwork status on the machine should say Relay: connected.

teamDsh.title: Team DSH
teamDsh.disclosure: A Team DSH is your team's machine, shared with others on its list. You see only the sessions you start; your team's admin can read every session from its encrypted archive.
teamDsh.none: None of this team's DSHs is open to you yet.
teamDsh.needsInvite: Ask your admin for an invite
teamDsh.joinHelp: Paste the invite link your admin gave you. This browser joins once, then sets a PIN of its own.
teamDsh.inviteInvalid: That is not an invite link. Paste the whole dshteamwork://join link your admin gave you.
teamDsh.inviteOtherServer: That invite is for another server.
teamDsh.browserUnsupported: This browser cannot keep the key a Team DSH needs. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, outside private browsing.
teamDsh.lockedHint: Too many wrong PINs. Ask your admin to unlock you on the Team DSH.
teamDsh.pitch: Run DSH on a machine your team owns, and work on it from the browser or the phone app.
teamDsh.featureMachineTitle: Nothing to set up on your own computer
teamDsh.featureMachineBody: The code, tools and dependencies live on the team's machine; open the console and start a session.
teamDsh.featureModelsBody: It signs in as the team, so its calls use the team's models and budgets, and provider keys never leave the server.
teamDsh.featurePrivateTitle: End-to-end encrypted, each to their own
teamDsh.featurePrivateBody: Your browser or phone talks to the machine end to end encrypted, behind a PIN, and you see only the sessions you start.
teamDsh.featureAuditTitle: An archive only the team can read
teamDsh.featureAuditBody: Every session is sealed to the team's audit key; the server keeps the archive without being able to open it.
teamDsh.notEnabledAdmin: Team DSH is enabled for some teams at a time, and this team does not have it yet. The platform operator enables it for a team: write to support to ask for it.
teamDsh.notEnabledMember: Team DSH is enabled for some teams at a time, and this team does not have it yet. The platform operator enables it for a team: ask your team's admin to request it.
teamDsh.setUp: No Team DSH yet? <link>Set one up</link> under Team assets.

myDsh.title: My DSH
myDsh.none: None of your computers has connected yet. Sign in to Teamwork in DSH on a computer, and it appears here.
myDsh.introTitle: Use your own computers from the browser
myDsh.intro: The DSH on each computer you signed in to Teamwork. Open one to pair this browser with it, then work in its sessions, end-to-end encrypted between this browser and that computer.
myDsh.openWebFailed: Could not open native DSH Web.
myDsh.offlineList: Its sessions are listed here once it is online.
myDsh.pairList: Pair this browser with it to see its sessions.
myDsh.unreachableList: Its sessions cannot be read right now.
myDsh.offlineHelp: Open DSH on that computer, signed in to Teamwork. This page carries on by itself once it connects.
myDsh.offlineUnpairedHelp: Open DSH on that computer, signed in to Teamwork, then pair this browser with it here.
myDsh.connectingHelp: Opening an end-to-end encrypted channel to the computer.
myDsh.pairHelp: On that computer, open the Teamwork panel in DSH and choose Devices, then make a pairing code and type it here.
myDsh.invalidCode: That code is wrong, spent or expired. Make a new one on the computer.
myDsh.otherComputer: That code was made on another computer.
myDsh.safetyHelp: The computer shows a code too. Continue only when both are the same.
myDsh.waitingApproval: Now approve this browser on the computer.
myDsh.refused: The computer did not accept this browser. Make a new code and try again.
myDsh.pairFailed: The connection to the computer broke before pairing finished. Make a new code on the computer and try again.
myDsh.lockedHint: Too many wrong PINs. On that computer, run /teamwork pin reset in DSH, then set a new PIN here.
myDsh.devicesHelp: Removing a phone or browser cuts it off at once, until it is paired again.
myDsh.noDevices: No phone or browser is paired with it.
myDsh.revokeConfirm: Remove {device}? It can no longer reach {name} until it is paired again.
myDsh.loadFailed: Your computers could not be read. Try again.
myDsh.revokeFailed: The device was not removed. Try again.
myDsh.removeComputerConfirm: Remove {name}? It is signed out of Teamwork at once, and every phone and browser paired with it is removed. Signing in on it again brings it back here, to be paired anew.
myDsh.removeComputerHelp: Lost this computer, or no longer use it? Removing it signs it out of Teamwork at once.
myDsh.removeComputerFailed: The computer was not removed. Try again.
myDsh.browserUnsupported: This browser cannot keep the key pairing needs. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, outside private browsing.
myDsh.nameHelp: Shown here, on your phones and in native DSH Web. It stays when the computer reconnects.
myDsh.webHelp: Opens this computer's own DSH Web in a new tab, through Teamwork.
myDsh.webOff: Turn on Native DSH Web in the computer's Teamwork panel, while the computer is online.

tasks.title: Automation tasks
tasks.help: Instructions this computer sends to a session at a time you choose, once or on a repeat.
tasks.pluginTooOld: Update DSH Teamwork on this computer to manage its automation tasks.
tasks.emptyHelp: Make one here, or ask the agent in any session, for example: “every weekday at 9:00, check the deployment status”.
tasks.notFound: This task is no longer on the computer.
tasks.deleteConfirm: Delete “{title}” and its delivery records? The sessions it sent to stay.

targets.new_once: A new session, reused each time

targetHelp.new_once: The first run starts a session; later runs continue it.
targetHelp.new: Every run starts in a fresh session.
targetHelp.session: Every run continues the session you pick.

tasks.customHelp: This task repeats on a custom rule, which is changed in DSH on the computer. Its name, instruction and session can be changed here.
tasks.historyHelp: A delivery means the instruction reached its session; open the session to see what the agent did.
tasks.name: Name
tasks.instructionPlaceholder: What the agent should do each time
tasks.cronHelp: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. For example 0 9 * * 1-5 is 9:00 on weekdays.
tasks.runsWhileOnline: A task runs only while DSH is running on this computer. One that was missed while it was off runs once when DSH starts again.

invalid.time_out_of_range: That time is out of range.

pages.title: Pages
pages.unavailable: This page is not available to you: it is private, was deleted, or you left its team.
pages.emptyHow: In a session on My DSH or a Team DSH, ask the agent to make a report, a deck or a dashboard and publish it as a page. It stays private to you until you share it.

empty.shared: Nobody has shared a page with you yet.
empty.all: No pages in this team yet.

pages.deleteConfirm: Delete "{title}" and every version of it? This cannot be undone.

usage.resolveHint: Record an estimate after checking supplier usage. This releases the reservation and retains the original evidence and your reason.
usage.reviewHint: This provider exceeded its reserved maximum. Confirm that its limits have been corrected before allowing further budgeted calls.
usage.resolvedPointsHint: Leave blank to use the captured rate. Enter 0 only after confirming no usage occurred. Points never change what your provider bills.
usage.reasonHint: Describe the supplier evidence and correction in 8–500 characters. Do not include credentials or conversation content.
usage.title: Usage
usage.description: The team's model calls, in tokens and points. Points are the team's own measure of cost: CNY 1 = 1,000 points at the reference rates, and budgets count them. With your own provider key, the provider still bills you directly.
usage.rateHint: CNY per million tokens. CNY 1 = 1,000 reference points. These rates do not charge a hosted balance.
usage.hostedRateHint: Hosted prices are published by the service. These prices also determine the points counted against your team budgets.
usage.unpricedHint: This model has no rates yet: members cannot call it until you set them.
usage.weightHint: Use these prices as internal usage weights rather than estimated supplier costs.
usage.empty: No model calls in this time range.
usage.accountingHint: Cached tokens are included in input; reasoning is included in output. A dash means unpriced or unconfirmed, not zero consumption.

budgets.memberUsageHint: Members with activity in this calendar period. Available points subtract active reservations; a dash means reconciliation is needed. Team and provider caps also apply.
budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.description: Set team and member spending ceilings. Everyone shares the applicable team limits.
budgets.empty: No budgets configured. Add a team cap or a default member allowance.
budgets.inherits: Uses the default member policy, if configured.
budgets.disabled: This policy does not restrict calls. Usage continues to be recorded.
budgets.timezonePending: Changes to {zone} at {at}; current spend is preserved.
budgets.unknownUsage: Unpriced or unconfirmed usage exists. Point availability may require reconciliation.
budgets.rules: Budgets are ceilings, not individual wallets. A new policy starts at creation; changes do not reset spend. Requests reserve their maximum supported usage before dispatch. Verified hard limits initially support direct DeepSeek text/function models; other providers remain reportable.
budgets.formHint: Changes preserve current-period usage. Member overrides replace that member's default policy for the same period.
budgets.blankUnlimited: Leave blank to apply token caps only. Zero blocks positive point consumption.
budgets.timezoneHint: Use an IANA zone such as Asia/Shanghai or UTC. Changes take effect at the next period boundary.
budgets.exists: This scope and period already have a budget. Close this dialog and edit its existing card.

notifyChoices.both: Team admins and the affected member

budgets.noticeHint: Alerts use your instance's SMTP service. In-app budget status works without email. Failed delivery never changes usage or limits.

memberModes.unlimited: No personal cap; team limits still apply
